I farm only 2.2 mu, and I am 62, so I will keep this year practical and steady. I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation because I know it well, it fits my land and water conditions, and it spreads my income across the year. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect yield, but I will not push inputs too high because my area is small and I care more about stable harvest than chasing the top yield. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate at the key stages, and manage weeds and disease with a few necessary sprays. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it yields better and stands better, give enough nitrogen for strong growth, and keep irrigation to the critical periods if rain is short. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage on a small plot and works well in this rotation. What I want is a reliable crop, manageable labor, and no wasted money.
